standard.title: Hermetic Compressors — Specification (Second Revision) (वायुरुद्ध संपीडक — विशिष्टि (दूसरा पुनरीक्षण))
standard.sector: Mechanical Engineering / Refrigeration and Air Conditioning

sectional_committee.name: Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard deals with the safety and performance requirements of hermetic sealed type standalone motor-compressors operating on a vapor compression cycle, suitable for low, medium, and high temperature applications based on reciprocating (including linear), rotary, and scroll pump mechanisms, including their internal protection systems, intended for household, commercial, and industrial equipment.
standard.scope: This standard deals with the safety and performance requirements of hermetic sealed type standalone motor-compressors operating on a vapor compression cycle, suitable for low, medium, and high temperature applications based on reciprocating (including linear), rotary, and scroll pump mechanisms, including their internal protection systems, intended for household, commercial, and industrial equipment.

version.current_version: Second Revision, December 2018 (Reaffirmed 2022) incorporating Amendment No. 1 (November 2020)

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). However, manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' on compressor housings and packaging. Under Quality Control Orders (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, many categories of hermetic compressors are under mandatory BIS certification to ensure safety, reliability, and energy efficiency across the country.
requirements: Hermetic standalone motor-compressor units must utilize either reciprocating (including linear reciprocating designs), rotary, or scroll pump mechanisms, suitable for low, medium, and high temperature applications.

Classifies compressors into three service envelopes based on evaporating temperature: LBP (-35°C to -10°C), MBP (-20°C to +10°C), and HBP (comfort AC at -5°C to +13.9°C, commercial heat pumps at -23.3°C to +12.8°C).
If a compressor is rated for a voltage range (e.g., 220–240 V), type and performance testing must be executed at the calculated mathematical mean voltage (e.g., 230 V).

To verify motor starting torque under equalized pressure conditions, the compressor is subjected to a Saturated Start Test with saturated evaporating/condensing temperatures set based on back-pressure grade: LBP at 15.0°C, MBP at 32.2°C, and HBP at 32.2°C.

The start test must be conducted for a duration of 3 hours or until the steel shell temperature stabilizes within ±5°C, using the higher rated voltage in dual-rated systems, while maintaining a minimum COP of 90.0% of its rated baseline.
The electrical insulation resistance measured between the motor windings and the compressor's steel housing must not be less than 2 MΩ.
The fully assembled steel housing must be tested pneumatically using dry air, nitrogen, or helium at a test pressure of 1.0 MPa (gauge) and must show zero leakage.
Calibrates housing test pressure to non-subcritical refrigerants: R-134a (CF3CH2F) at 6.5 MPa (65 Bar), R-22 (CHClF2) at 10.5 MPa (105 Bar), and R-600a (CH(CH3)3) at 3.5 MPa (35 Bar).
If a specialized compressor's design operating envelope lies outside standard parameters, testing must be carried out at the worst-case condition within the manufacturer's defined operating envelope.

Under the November 2020 amendment, starting tests are restricted to single-phase induction motor compressors only, and units must start and run at the minimum of the voltage range defined by the compressor specification.

Final observed or calculated test and analytical values must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value.
